mainTopic: How a doubtful נזיר completes his offerings: the surviving partner's method in the dispute of רבי יהושע and בן זומא, and the נזיר who is both a possible טמא מת and a possible מצורע
overview: The previous משנה covered two נזירים where one became טמא but nobody knows which one. This משנה asks what the survivor does if one of them dies. רבי יהושע says the survivor finds a new partner who takes a conditional נזירות vow, and the two bring conditional offerings over two rounds of thirty days. בן זומא objects that nobody will agree to such a vow. Instead, the survivor brings a bird חטאת and an animal עולה on condition, and thirty days later brings his purity offerings. רבי יהושע complains that this splits the offerings into halves, but the חכמים side with בן זומא. The גמרא explains that רבי יהושע only said this to sharpen his students, and רב נחמן jokes that the first animal's innards would spoil if they had to wait. A new משנה then describes a נזיר who is possibly טמא מת and possibly a confirmed מצורע. He may eat קדשים after sixty days and finishes his נזירות after 120 days, because a doubtful מצורע's shaving does not override the נזיר's ban on shaving.

steps.title: One of the two נזירים dies: find a partner
steps.stepSummary: If one of the two doubtful נזירים dies, רבי יהושע says the survivor should ask someone from the marketplace to take a נזירות vow that matches his own.
steps.simpleTranslation: If one of them died, רבי יהושע said: he should ask someone from the marketplace to vow to be a נזיר corresponding to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה opens a new case. One of the two נזירים from the earlier case has died, and רבי יהושע gives his solution: the survivor finds a new partner.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before, the two נזירים could split the offerings between them with conditions. Now one has died, so the survivor has nobody to share the doubt with. רבי יהושע's fix is to bring in a stranger who takes on נזירות so the conditional system can still work.

keyTerms.meaning: Marketplace; here it means some ordinary person who is not a נזיר
Corresponding to him, matching his situation
He will vow to become a נזיר

steps.confusionAlert: "One of them" means one of the two נזירים from the previous משנה, where one became טמא and nobody knows which. This משנה does not explain that background again.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
If one of them died,
phrases.notes: "Them" is the two נזירים from the last משנה, one of whom became טמא without anyone knowing which.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua said:
He should ask someone from the marketplace
to vow to be a nazir corresponding to him.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵת אֶחָד מֵהֶן, אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the משנה with a new case that builds on the previous משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The survivor asks an outsider to take a נזירות vow that matches his own, so the offerings can still be brought with conditions.

steps.title: The wording of the partner's conditional vow
steps.stepSummary: The survivor tells the partner: if I was טמא, you are a נזיר starting now; if I was טהור, your נזירות starts after thirty days.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he says: If I was impure, you are a נזיר right away. And if I was pure, you are a נזיר after thirty days.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה spells out the exact condition the partner's vow depends on. This sets up the timing for the offerings in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The partner's start date depends on the survivor's unknown status. If the survivor was טמא, he must restart his נזירות now, so the partner starts now too and they move together. If the survivor was טהור, his own נזירות ends in thirty days, so the partner's thirty days begin only then.

keyTerms.meaning: Impure, here from contact with a dead body

phrases.english: And he says: If I was impure,
you are hereby a nazir immediately;
and if I was pure,

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי אַתָּה נָזִיר אַחַר שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם.
phrases.english: you are hereby a nazir after thirty days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the details of the vow mentioned in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The partner's נזירות starts immediately if the survivor was טמא, and after thirty days if he was טהור.

steps.title: After the first thirty days: offerings of impurity and of purity
steps.stepSummary: After thirty days they bring both a קרבן טומאה and a קרבן טהרה, and the survivor states who each offering belongs to in each possibility.
steps.simpleTranslation: They count thirty days and bring an impurity offering and a purity offering. He says: If I am the impure one, the impurity offering is mine and the purity offering is yours. If I am the pure one, the purity offering is mine and the impurity offering is brought because of the doubt.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה describes the first round of offerings. The survivor sets a condition that assigns each offering to the right person, whichever way the truth turns out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the survivor was טמא, he needs the impurity offering, and the partner, who started right away, has finished thirty days and needs the purity offering. If the survivor was טהור, his own thirty days are done, so the purity offering is his, and the impurity offering is only there because of the doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: The offering a נזיר brings after becoming טמא
The offering a נזיר brings when he finishes his נזירות in purity
Brought out of doubt, with uncertain status

phrases.english: And they count thirty days,
and bring an offering of impurity and an offering of purity.
And he says: If I am the impure one,

phrases.aramaic: קׇרְבַּן טוּמְאָה שֶׁלִּי, וְקׇרְבַּן טׇהֳרָה שֶׁלְּךָ.
phrases.english: the offering of impurity is mine, and the offering of purity is yours.
And if I am the pure one,

phrases.aramaic: קׇרְבַּן טׇהֳרָה שֶׁלִּי, וְקׇרְבַּן טוּמְאָה בְּסָפֵק.
phrases.english: the offering of purity is mine, and the offering of impurity is of uncertain status.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְסוֹפְרִין שְׁלֹשִׁים, וּמְבִיאִין קׇרְבַּן טוּמְאָה וְקׇרְבַּן טׇהֳרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Carries out the first stage of the plan set up by the vow in step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: At thirty days both offerings are brought, and a stated condition assigns each one to the right person in either case.

steps.title: After the second thirty days: one more purity offering
steps.stepSummary: After another thirty days they bring one more קרבן טהרה. In either case, the earlier offerings and this new one now cover both people.
steps.simpleTranslation: They count another thirty days and bring a purity offering. He says: If I was the impure one, the impurity offering was mine, the purity offering was yours, and this is my purity offering. If I was the pure one, the purity offering was mine, the impurity offering was brought because of the doubt, and this is your purity offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes רבי יהושע's procedure with a second round. The survivor explains how this last purity offering fits each possibility.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the survivor was טמא, he restarted his נזירות at day thirty, so now he finishes and brings his own purity offering. If he was טהור, the partner only began at day thirty, so this purity offering is the partner's. Either way, everyone has brought exactly what he needs.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהושע's method uses a partner and two thirty-day rounds. Every offering gets assigned to the right person no matter who was really טמא.

phrases.english: And they count another thirty days,
and bring an offering of purity,
and he says: If I was the impure one,
the offering of impurity was mine,
phrases.notes: He means the impurity offering they brought back at the first thirty days.

phrases.english: and the offering of purity was yours,
and this is my offering of purity.
And if I was the pure one,
the offering of purity was mine,
and the offering of impurity was of uncertain status,
and this is your offering of purity.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְסוֹפְרִים שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם, וּמְבִיאִין קׇרְבַּן טׇהֳרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the procedure that began in step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A second purity offering after another thirty days completes what both people need, whichever one was טמא.

steps.title: בן זומא: who would agree to such a vow?
steps.stepSummary: בן זומא challenges רבי יהושע: who would ever agree to become a נזיר just to help this person?
steps.simpleTranslation: בן זומא said to him: And who will listen to him and vow to be a נזיר corresponding to him?
steps.whatsHappening: בן זומא attacks רבי יהושע's method on practical grounds. The question is really a challenge: nobody will agree to do this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בן זומא does not say the procedure is wrong in theory. His point is that it depends on a stranger agreeing to take on נזירות, with no wine and no haircuts, possibly for a long time. A rule that depends on that is not realistic.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who argues with רבי יהושע here
And who will listen to him?

phrases.english: Ben Zoma said to him:
And who will listen to him
to vow to be a nazir corresponding to him?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ בֶּן זוֹמָא: וּמִי שׁוֹמֵעַ לוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the basic idea of רבי יהושע's procedure from step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהושע's requirement to find a partner who takes on נזירות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The method depends on an outsider willingly taking a burdensome vow, which is not a realistic thing to expect.

steps.title: בן זומא's alternative: a bird חטאת and an animal עולה
steps.stepSummary: Instead, the survivor brings a bird חטאת and an animal עולה with a condition: if he was טמא, the חטאת is his obligation and the עולה is a gift; if he was טהור, the עולה is his obligation and the חטאת is brought because of the doubt.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he brings a bird sin-offering and an animal burnt-offering, and says: If I was impure, the sin-offering is my obligation and the burnt-offering is a gift. And if I was pure, the burnt-offering is my obligation and the sin-offering is brought because of the doubt.
steps.whatsHappening: בן זומא offers his own method that needs no partner. The survivor covers both possibilities himself with one set of offerings and a stated condition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A טמא נזיר brings a bird חטאת, and a טהור נזיר brings an animal עולה. By bringing a bird חטאת together with an animal עולה, the survivor covers both cases. Whichever offering turns out not to be needed is either a voluntary gift (the עולה) or brought because of the doubt (the חטאת).

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; brings in a different approach

steps.whatToRemember: There are two approaches. רבי יהושע uses a partner and two rounds of thirty days. בן זומא lets the survivor handle it alone with a bird חטאת and an animal עולה brought on condition.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא: מֵבִיא חַטַּאת הָעוֹף וְעוֹלַת בְּהֵמָה,
phrases.english: Rather, he brings a bird sin-offering and an animal burnt-offering,
and says: If I was impure,
the sin-offering is for my obligation, and the burnt-offering is a gift offering.
And if I was pure,
the burnt-offering is for my obligation, and the sin-offering is of uncertain status.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: מֵבִיא חַטַּאת הָעוֹף וְעוֹלַת בְּהֵמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives בן זומא's replacement procedure after his challenge in step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The survivor brings a bird חטאת and an animal עולה on condition, covering both the טמא and the טהור possibilities without a partner.

steps.title: After thirty days he brings purity offerings and assigns each burnt offering by a condition
steps.stepSummary: The survivor counts thirty days and brings a קרבן טהרה. If he was טמא, the first עולה was a gift and the new one is his obligation. If he was טהור, the first עולה was his obligation, the new one is a gift, and the other new offerings complete his set.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then he counts thirty days and brings the purity offerings. He says: If I was impure, the first burnt offering was a gift and this one is my obligation. If I was pure, the first burnt offering was my obligation, this one is a gift, and these are the rest of my offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes בן זומא's plan. The survivor now brings his purity offerings and states a condition so that they count correctly in either case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If he was טמא, he had to restart his thirty days, so only the new purity offerings count, and the earlier animal עולה becomes a gift. If he was טהור, the earlier עולה already counted as his purity עולה. In that case the new עולה is extra, and the new חטאת and שלמים complete his set. Either way, every required offering gets brought.

keyTerms.meaning: The set of offerings a נזיר brings when he finishes his נזירות in purity

steps.whatToRemember: בן זומא's method works without a partner. Conditional statements make every offering count, whichever way the doubt turns out.

phrases.english: And he counts thirty days,
and brings an offering of purity,
and says: If I was impure,
the first burnt offering is a gift, and this one is the obligation.
phrases.notes: The 'first burnt offering' is the animal עולה from the step before, which was brought together with the bird חטאת.

phrases.english: And if I was pure,
the first burnt offering is the obligation, and this one is a gift,
and this is the rest of my offerings.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְסוֹפֵר שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם, וּמֵבִיא קׇרְבַּן טׇהֳרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the conditional-offering method that בן זומא began in step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After thirty days the survivor brings purity offerings and assigns the two עולות conditionally, so that his obligation is met in either case.

steps.title: רבי יהושע objects that the offerings come in two parts
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע points out a problem with בן זומא's plan. If the survivor was טהור, his purity offerings end up split: the עולה came first, and the rest came thirty days later.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע said: It turns out that this person brings his offerings in halves.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע challenges בן זומא's method. It causes the purity offerings to be brought in two separate parts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the טהור case, the first עולה counts as the purity עולה, but the חטאת and שלמים come thirty days later. רבי יהושע assumes that a נזיר's set of offerings should come together. That makes this split look like a flaw.

keyTerms.meaning: It turns out (pointing to a result of the plan)
In halves, meaning in separate stages

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua said:
It turns out that this one brings his offerings in halves.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the method just laid out in steps 6 and 7.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the טהור case the עולה is separated from the rest of the purity offerings by thirty days, so the offerings are not brought together.

steps.title: The חכמים agree with בן זומא
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים accept בן זומא's method, even with רבי יהושע's objection.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the חכמים agreed with בן זומא.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends with the ruling: the חכמים side with בן זומא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים are not bothered by the offerings being brought in two parts. So the halves objection does not cancel the method. This sets up the גמרא's question about why רבי יהושע raised it at all.
steps.whatToRemember: The halacha follows בן זומא: the survivor uses conditional offerings and needs no partner.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הוֹדוּ לוֹ חֲכָמִים לְבֶן זוֹמָא.
phrases.english: But the Sages agreed with ben Zoma.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל הוֹדוּ לוֹ חֲכָמִים לְבֶן זוֹמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the dispute by rejecting רבי יהושע's objection in practice.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The חכמים accept בן זומא's method, and bringing the offerings in stages is acceptable.

steps.title: What is wrong with bringing them in stages?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יהושע: why not simply bring the offerings in two parts?
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: So let him bring them that way!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now opens its discussion. It questions רבי יהושע's objection from the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא sees no rule forbidding a נזיר from bringing his offerings at different times. If so, the 'halves' objection seems to have no basis.

phrases.english: GEMARA: So let him bring them!
phrases.notes: Meaning: let him bring the offerings in two parts. What's the problem?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the basis of רבי יהושע's objection in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהושע's objection about offerings brought in halves
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Nothing forbids bringing the offerings in stages, so the objection seems empty.

steps.title: רבי יהושע only said it to sharpen the students
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of שמואל answers that רבי יהושע did not truly hold this. He said it to test his students.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: רבי יהושע said this only to sharpen the students with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question. רבי יהושע's objection was a teaching test, not a real ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question from step 10 stays correct: bringing offerings in stages really is fine. רבי יהושע raised the point to see whether his students would know that it is allowed.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't read רבי יהושע's comment as a real ruling that offerings may not be split. The גמרא says it was only a test.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
Rabbi Yehoshua did not say it
except to sharpen the students with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אֶלָּא לְחַדֵּד בָּהּ אֶת הַתַּלְמִידִים
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the speaker's intent: the statement was a test, not a ruling.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהושע truly held that a נזיר's offerings may not be brought in stages.
steps.terutzMaskana: Bringing the offerings in stages is allowed. רבי יהושע only wanted to test whether his students knew this.

steps.title: רב נחמן: what would רבי יהושע do with the innards?
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן makes a light remark. Insisting that all the offerings come together would mean keeping the first animal's innards for thirty days, and they would spoil.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: What should רבי יהושע do with his innards so that they do not spoil?
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן adds a humorous point. It shows that רבי יהושע's objection could not have been meant seriously.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The only way to keep the offerings 'together' would be to wait thirty days to finish the first עולה, holding its innards that whole time. That is clearly impossible. So the objection must have been a test, which backs up שמואל's answer.
steps.whatToRemember: The גמרא concludes that bringing a נזיר's offerings in stages is fine. רבי יהושע's 'halves' objection was not a real halachic concern.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said:
What should Rabbi Yehoshua do for him
with the innards, so that they not spoil?
phrases.notes: He means the innards of the first עולה, which would have to wait thirty days if everything had to be brought together.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי לֶיעְבֵּיד לֵיהּ רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ לְדַקַּיָּה דְּלָא לֵיסְרוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports שמואל's answer by showing that the objection cannot be taken literally.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's claim that רבי יהושע's objection was only a test for the students
steps.raayaSupportSource: The practical impossibility of keeping the first עולה's innards for thirty days without spoiling

steps.title: The doubly-doubtful נזיר may eat קדשים after sixty days
steps.stepSummary: The משנה presents a נזיר who is possibly טמא מת and possibly a confirmed מצורע. It rules that he may eat קדשים only after sixty days.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A נזיר who was possibly impure from a dead body, and possibly a confirmed מצורע, may eat holy offerings after sixty days.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה starts. It describes a נזיר with two doubts and says when he may eat קדשים again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מצורע must shave twice and cannot eat קדשים until he finishes his purification. A נזיר may not shave. Since his צרעת is only a doubt, he waits thirty days before each shaving: one at day 30 and one at day 60. After the second shaving he brings his offerings and may eat קדשים.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for מתניתין, 'our משנה.' It marks the start of a new משנה.
A doubt; we do not know if it is true.
A confirmed מצורע, not just one who is put aside to be checked.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two numbers. Sixty days is only for eating קדשים, which depends on finishing the מצורע process. Drinking wine and becoming טמא wait until 120 days, as the next step explains.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
A nazirite who was impure as a matter of doubt
and a confirmed leper as a matter of doubt
may eat sacrificial food
after sixty days.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ נָזִיר שֶׁהָיָה טָמֵא בְּסָפֵק וּמוּחְלָט בְּסָפֵק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the גמרא's discussion of בן זומא's method ended in step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A נזיר who is possibly טמא מת and possibly a confirmed מצורע may eat קדשים only after sixty days.

steps.title: He may drink wine and become impure only after 120 days
steps.stepSummary: The same נזיר may drink wine and become טמא from the dead only after 120 days.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he may drink wine and become impure from the dead only after 120 days.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a second, longer waiting time. This is when this נזיר's נזירות is fully over.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Maybe he really was a מצורע, so his first two shavings (day 30 and day 60) count only for צרעת. He needs another thirty days of נזירות and a shaving at day 90. But maybe he was also טמא מת, so that shaving counts for the טומאה. He then needs thirty more days of clean נזירות, which brings him to day 120.

keyTerms.meaning: Drinks wine, which a נזיר may not do during his נזירות.
Becomes impure from the dead, which a נזיר may not do.

phrases.english: And he may drink wine,
and become impure from the dead,
after 120 days.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְשׁוֹתֶה יַיִן, וּמִטַּמֵּא לַמֵּתִים אַחַר מֵאָה וְעֶשְׂרִים יוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second waiting time for the same נזיר, after the sixty days for קדשים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The נזיר's restrictions on wine and טומאה end only after 120 days.

steps.title: Why he must wait: a doubtful מצורע's shaving does not override נזירות
steps.stepSummary: The משנה explains its numbers. The shaving of a מצורע overrides the נזיר's ban on shaving only when he is definitely a מצורע. When it is only a doubt, it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because the shaving for צרעת overrides the shaving ban of a נזיר when he is definitely a מצורע. But when it is a doubt, it does not override.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the reason for the long waits in the last two steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A sure מצורע would shave right away and again a week later, even though he is a נזיר. Here the צרעת is only a doubt, so it cannot push aside the ban on shaving. He must wait until a shaving is allowed anyway, at the end of a thirty-day term. That is why everything moves in thirty-day blocks.

keyTerms.meaning: Shaving, required both for a נזיר and for a מצורע.
The skin mark of צרעת. Here it stands for the מצורע's shaving.

steps.whatToRemember: Only a definite מצורע may shave during נזירות. A doubtful one must wait for thirty-day breaks. This gives 60 days until he may eat קדשים and 120 days until his נזירות is over.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule explains why the משנה uses thirty-day blocks and not the usual seven days of a מצורע's process.
